original_question: A group is boundedly acyclic if its bounded cohomology with trivial real coefficients vanishes in all positive degrees. Is every branch group boundedly acyclic?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.116 in the "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)" section of The Kourovka Notebook; arXiv:1401.0300 is this notebook itself, and the exact matching target is that open problem. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the official problem almost verbatim: it states the notebook's definition of boundedly acyclic and asks whether every branch group has that property. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: To make the question fully stand-alone, spell out the cohomological form explicitly: for every branch group G and every integer n ≥ 1, require H_b^n(G; R) = 0. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
Specify that the coefficient module is R with the trivial G-action. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Specify what class of groups is meant by "branch group"; the notebook uses the standard term without unpacking it, so a stand-alone version should fix the standard meaning rather than leave it implicit.

Do not add extra hypotheses such as finitely generated, just-infinite, regular branch, weakly branch, or torsion; the notebook problem asks about every branch group. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Let G be a branch group in the standard sense. Must H_b^n(G; R) = 0 for every integer n ≥ 1, where R is viewed as a trivial G-module? Equivalently, is every branch group boundedly acyclic? ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
equivalent_formulation: Is every branch group boundedly acyclic? ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Your draft is therefore already very close to paper-faithful; the only refinements needed are to make the trivial coefficient module, the quantifier n ≥ 1, and the meaning of "branch group" explicit, without broadening the scope beyond the notebook's universal quantifier over branch groups. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300))
